source.title: Open Problem: Is There an Online Learning Algorithm That Learns Whenever Online Learning Is Possible?

accepted.question_text: Consider realizable binary online learning over a nonempty instance space X with measurable target concepts f*: X → {0,1}. At each time t, after observing the past labeled examples (X_s, f*(X_s)) for s < t and the current instance X_t, an online learning algorithm predicts a label in {0,1}; its mistakes are the times when the prediction differs from f*(X_t). For a possibly random instance sequence X independent of the learner's internal randomness, weak universal consistency under X means that, for every measurable f*, the expected number of mistakes through time T is o(T), while strong universal consistency under X means that, for every measurable f*, the number of mistakes through time T is o(T) almost surely. Universal online learning is possible under X if some online learning algorithm has the corresponding universal consistency property under X. Does there exist a single optimistically universal online learning algorithm, meaning a single algorithm that is weakly, respectively strongly, universally consistent under every instance sequence X for which weak, respectively strong, universal online learning is possible under X?

evidence.quote: One of the most classical topics in learning theory is online learning, wherein a learning algorithm observes a stream of data points X_t from a space X, and for each time t ∈ N it makes a prediction Ŷ_t ∈ {0,1}, after which it observes the target label Y_t ∈ {0,1}. The prediction Ŷ_t may depend on the past observations ((X_s,Y_s),s<t) and X_t, but nothing else: that is, Ŷ_t = f_t(X_{1:(t−1)},Y_{1:(t−1)},X_t) for a (possibly randomized) function f_t. The objective is to make few mistakes: that is, few times t for which Ŷ_t ≠ Y_t. In particular, we are most interested in achieving a number of mistakes among {(X_t,Y_t)}_{t≤T} growing sublinearly in T: that is, o(T) mistakes.

Definition 1 For a (possibly random) sequence X = {X_t}_{t∈N}, an online learning algorithm f_t : X^{t−1} × {0,1}^{t−1} × X → {0,1} (possibly randomized, independent of X) is weakly universally consistent under X if, for every (measurable) f* : X → {0,1}, E[∑_{t=1}^T 1[f_t(X_{1:(t−1)},f*(X_{1:(t−1)}),X_t) ≠ f*(X_t)]] = o(T), and is strongly universally consistent under X if, for every (measurable) f* : X → {0,1}, ∑_{t=1}^T 1[f_t(X_{1:(t−1)},f*(X_{1:(t−1)}),X_t) ≠ f*(X_t)] = o(T) (a.s.).

Definition 2 For a (possibly random) sequence X, we say (weak/strong) universal online learning is possible under X if there exists an online learning algorithm that is (weakly/strongly) universally consistent under X.

Definition 3 An online learning algorithm is optimistically (weakly/strongly) universal if it is (weakly/strongly) universally consistent under every X such that (weak/strong) universal online learning is possible under X.
Open Problem 1 Does there exist an optimistically universal online learning algorithm? (in either the weak or strong sense)

accepted.question_text: In realizable binary online learning with arbitrary measurable target concepts f*: X → {0,1}, say that weak universal online learning is possible under a possibly random instance sequence X if some online learning algorithm has expected total mistakes o(T) through time T for every measurable f*. Let C_w be the family of all possibly random sequences X = {X_t}_{t∈N} such that every disjoint sequence {A_i}_{i∈N} of measurable sets satisfies E[|{i ∈ N : {X_1,...,X_T} intersects A_i}|] = o(T). Is C_w exactly equal to the set of all instance sequences X such that weak universal online learning is possible under X?
accepted.context_brief: Weak universal online learning characterization by C_w

evidence.quote: Definition 1 For a (possibly random) sequence X = {X_t}_{t∈N}, an online learning algorithm f_t : X^{t−1} × {0,1}^{t−1} × X → {0,1} (possibly randomized, independent of X) is weakly universally consistent under X if, for every (measurable) f* : X → {0,1}, E[∑_{t=1}^T 1[f_t(X_{1:(t−1)},f*(X_{1:(t−1)}),X_t) ≠ f*(X_t)]] = o(T).

Definition 2 For a (possibly random) sequence X, we say (weak/strong) universal online learning is possible under X if there exists an online learning algorithm that is (weakly/strongly) universally consistent under X.
Let C_w denote the family of all (possibly random) sequences X = {X_t}_{t∈N} such that every disjoint sequence {A_i}_{i∈N} of measurable sets satisfies E[|{i ∈ N : X_{1:T} ∩ A_i ≠ ∅}|] = o(T).
Open Problem 2 • Is C_w equal to the set of all X such that weak universal online learning is possible under X?

Thus, the case that remains open in Open Problem 2 concerns whether X ∈ C_w or X ∈ C_s are sufficient conditions for weak or strong, respectively, universal online learning to be possible under X for uncountable X and general (random) sequences X.
